newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel oil steady, Russian pressured.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel oil steady, Russian pressured.

text.p: European low sulphur straight-run prices were steady to higher on Thursday and sellers said they could charge at the top end of the range with little supply available.
Russian high sulphur straight-run, however, was said distressed with several cargoes still unsold and little buying interest from refiners.
Traders said 6,000 tonnes of low sulphur straight-run was traded at $112 fob on Thursday following a deal for a 25,000-tonne end month loader sold by a refiner at $109 fob late on Wednesday.
One other seller was at $110 and two others at $112, almost unchanged from a day earlier.

"There's four buyers showing interest. Their numbers are still low, in the $106/$107 range, but if they recognise that there's not that much product is left, the numbers will go higher" one of the sellers said.

Russian high sulphur straight-run was softer, with levels for M-100 put at two means, possibly as high as $2 over, depending on dates and quality. E-4 was said close to the three means quote falt, fetching no premiums.
"It's a quiet depressed market with a fair amount of cargoes on the water and with very limited buying especially from refiners," one trader said.
"The buyers are holding back also with crude going all over the place and there's two to three cargoes of E-4 available in the next four to five days and a little bit more of M-100," he said.
A second trader said: "There's no real interest in Russian material. Refinery margins are better now, they see it is better to run crude instead of feedstocks."

There was unconfirmed talk of an E-4 trading on Thursday. An M-100 cargo was said to have changed hands late on Wednesday between two means and $2.50 over, or the same price or a little lower than what bunker spec fetched that day.
But the story was different in the Med, where avails of Russian straight-run are low.
Traders said M-100 was traded late on Wednesday at high cif Med +$3, or steady. The cargo was sold by a trader to a refiner, the traders added.
